head.reference: MALE heads have comb-like racemes; FEMALE heads have hard short bur-like clusters, formed by stiffened glumes and floral branches, not Cenchrus fused bristle burs. Most plants dioecious, occasionally monoecious. Broad key must not eliminate female form.

sexual_system.reference: Usually dioecious, rarely monoecious; sexes have quite different heads. Do not label it as male/female zones on the same flowerhead.

diagnostic_checks.look: Find the MALE and FEMALE heads, even if on different plants
diagnostic_checks.check: Buffalograss is usually DIOECIOUS, with male and female inflorescences on separate plants (occasionally both on one). MALE heads carry 1–4 comb-like branches with orderly two-rowed spikelets, while FEMALE seed-bearing clusters are short, hard bur-like units often tucked among leaves.
diagnostic_checks.compare: Blue grama has curved comb-like branches but not this striking female bur-like head; Cenchrus sandbur has a spiny fused bristle involucre rather than a buffalograss female branched reproductive cluster.
diagnostic_checks.certainty: Kew GrassBase male/female morphology; each photo must have authenticated sex and intact attachment

diagnostic_checks.look: Open a FEMALE cluster without mistaking it for spiny sandbur
diagnostic_checks.check: Female branches contain normally 2–5 ONE-FLORET spikelets; thickened upper glumes and the branch axis form a small hardened globular toothed unit. Glume tips can have three teeth but it is NOT a Cenchrus burr of fused bristles.
diagnostic_checks.compare: Sandbur involucres have bristle-derived spines surrounding several spikelets; buffalograss female clusters have hardened glumes and branching axes.
diagnostic_checks.certainty: Kew / FNA-linked source checked, opened female branch with ruler still pending

diagnostic_checks.look: Follow a ground-level STOLON to a rooted node and inner ligule

diagnostic_checks.compare: Bermudagrass has both long scaly underground rhizomes and surface stolons, with typically 4–6 slender fingers on flowering culms.
diagnostic_checks.certainty: Regional flora / Kew morphology; rooted runner and collar macro not yet checked

Texas grama has several much shorter bristly clustered branches. Sideoats has many short side branches all the way down a long stem.
